[element-std-ref]
=== `<std-ref>` Standard Reference Designation

`<std-ref>` contains the value (as a string) of one standard reference designator, for example, “`ISO 9001:2015`”. This designator typically consists of an originator or SDO-abbreviated name (e.g., “`ISO`”) and a standard number or identifier (such as “`9001`”), and it may also include a year (such as “`2015`”) or other information that uniquely identifies a given standard.

#### Usage/Remarks
The <<element-std-ref,`<std-ref>`>> element can be used in two contexts: Within the metadata of a standard (inside <<element-std-meta,`<std-meta>`>> or <<element-iso-meta,`<iso-meta>`>> or similar), the standard designation element <<element-std-ref,`<std-ref>`>> names a designator for the current standard and is typically provided twice, once in dated and once in undated form. Outside the metadata, when a standard is mentioned within the prose of a standards document, the element <<element-std,`<std>`>> is used to hold the designation and other information for the standard being cited. Inside that <<element-std,`<std>`>> element, the element <<element-std-ref,`<std-ref>`>> may be used to identify the designator of the cited standard and/or separate it from other information concerning the standard, such as the standard’s title.
##### Best Practice Content

Although many elements are allowed inside a `<std-ref>`, Best Practice is to make the content just text. For Best Practice, the elements that are allowed in `<std-ref>` should be tagged as part of the <<element-std-ident,`<std-ident>`>> element, leaving <<element-std-ref,`<std-ref>`>> as a simple string.
For Best Practice, a deep link to another standard (in which a figure, table, or similar internal structure from the other standard is the target of the link) should be tagged using the element <<element-std,`<std>`>> rather than by using `<std-ref>`.
##### Citing a Correction or Amendment Best Practice

When a correction or amendment is referenced, it is Best Practice to include the full reference in `<std-ref>`, e.g.
[source,xml]
....
<std-ref>ISO/IEC 1989: 2002/Cor.3:2009</std-ref>
....
#### Type Attribute

The several forms of reference designation (dated, short, etc.) should be distinguished using the <<attribute-type,`@type`>> attribute.
#### Redundant in Metadata

Strictly speaking, the standard reference designation `<std-ref>` that is part of the metadata of a standards document can almost always be constructed from information present in the <<element-std-ident,`<std-ident>`>> element, with the insertion of appropriate spacing and separators. But even as part of the metadata, it can be convenient to have a precombined form of the identifier all together in one place.
#### Standard Designator Type (<<attribute-type,`@type`>>)

The <<attribute-type,`@type`>> attribute describes standard designator (for example, “`dated`”, “`undated`”, or “`short`”). <<attribute-type,`@type`>> has as its values a fixed list of designation types. To record a designation type that is not one of the listed types, you can use <<attribute-custom-type,`@custom-type`>> to describe the actual type. Set the value of <<attribute-type,`@type`>> to “`custom`” and also use <<attribute-custom-type,`@custom-type`>> to name type you require.

#### Attributes

* <<attribute-custom-type,`@custom-type`>>
* <<attribute-type,`@type`>>
#### Base Attributes

* <<attribute-id,`@id`>>
* <<attribute-xml-base,`@xml:base`>>

#### Description

Any combination of: Text, numbers, or special characters <<element-originator,`<originator>`>> <<element-originator,Originator>> <<element-doc-type,`<doc-type>`>> <<element-doc-type,Document Type>> <<element-doc-number,`<doc-number>`>> <<element-doc-number,Document Number>> <<element-part-number,`<part-number>`>> <<element-part-number,Part Number of a Multipart Document>> <<element-edition,`<edition>`>> <<element-edition,Edition Number>> <<element-isbn,`<isbn>`>> <<element-isbn,ISBN>> <<element-suppl-type,`<suppl-type>`>> <<element-suppl-type,Supplement Type>> <<element-suppl-number,`<suppl-number>`>> <<element-suppl-number,Supplement Number>> <<element-suppl-version,`<suppl-version>`>> <<element-suppl-version,Supplement Version>> <<element-version,`<version>`>> <<element-version,Version Indicator>> <<element-year,`<year>`>> <<element-year,Year>>
#### Content Model

[source,xml]
....
<!ELEMENT  std-ref      (#PCDATA %std-ref-elements;)*                >
....
#### Expanded Content Model

(#PCDATA | originator | doc-type | doc-number | part-number | edition | isbn | suppl-type | suppl-number | suppl-version | version | year)*

#### Tagged Samples

#### In metadata of standard

[source,xml]
....
...
<iso-meta>
 ...
 <content-language>en</content-language>
 <std-ref type="undated">ISO 2560</std-ref>
 <std-ref type="dated">ISO 2560:2009</std-ref>
 <doc-ref>ISO 2560:2009(en)</doc-ref>
 <release-date iso-8601-date="2009-05-30" 
   date-type="published">2009-05-30</release-date>
 ...  
</iso-meta>
...
....
#### Standard named in “Normative references” section

[source,xml]
....
...
<ref>
 <std><std-ref type="undated">ISO/IEC&#x00A0;17025</std-ref>, 
  <title>General requirements for the competence of testing 
   and calibration laboratories</title></std>
</ref>
...
<ref>
 <std><std-ref type="dated">ISO&#x00A0;15223&#x2011;1:2012</std-ref>, 
  <title>Medical devices&#x00A0;&#x2014; Symbols to be used 
   with medical device labels, labelling and information 
   to be supplied&#x00A0;&#x2014; Part&#x00A0;1: General 
   requirements</title></std>
</ref>
...
....
#### Standard named in text

[source,xml]
....
...
<non-normative-note>
 <label>NOTE</label>
 <p>Guidance on this issue may be found in 
  <std><std-ref type="short">EN&#x00A0;1006</std-ref></std> (see 
  Bibliography [<xref rid="bib-3">3</xref>]).</p>
</non-normative-note>
<p>... complying with 
 <std><std-ref type="dated">ISO&#x00A0;5356&#x2011;1</std-ref></std>.</p>
...
....
#### Standard named in “Bibliographic references” section

[source,xml]
....
...
<ref content-type="standard" id="ref3">
 <label>[3]</label>
 <std><std-ref type="undated">EN&#x00A0;1006</std-ref>, 
  <title>Advanced technical ceramics&#x00A0;&#x2014;Monolithic 
   ceramics&#x00A0;&#x2014; Guidance on the selection of test 
   pieces for the evaluation of properties</title></std>
</ref>
...
<ref content-type="standard" id="ref9">
 <label>[9]</label>
 <std><std-ref type="undated">ISO&#x00A0;13399 (all parts)</std-ref>, 
  <title>Cutting tool data representation and exchange</title></std>
</ref>
...
....
